paragraphs.paragraph_en: Multivariate time series forecasting underpins safety-critical scheduling across smart power grids, cloud clusters, and automated manufacturing. In these operational settings, control systems rely on multi-horizon predictions to balance supply fluctuations and prevent cascading overload. However, field sensors routinely operate under abrupt regime shifts, irregular sampling intervals, and high-frequency measurement noise. Failing to accommodate such non-stationary disturbances degrades long-range forecast reliability and triggers costly control oscillations.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Recent deep forecasters have substantially reduced long-horizon error by replacing point-wise attention with sub-series patch tokenization and frequency-domain decomposition. These architectures effectively capture recurring seasonal patterns when training and test sequences share stationary statistical moments. Yet they implicitly assume that inter-channel correlations and spectral energy distributions remain time-invariant across the prediction window. When external shocks alter underlying system dynamics, this stationarity assumption collapses, causing frozen spectral filters to project outdated trends.

paragraphs.paragraph_intent_zh: 我这一段想深入剖析现有方法在特定难题（如非平稳突变、长程自回归误差累积、Sim-to-Real 接触失配）上为什么会失效，把机理讲透。

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Bridging non-stationary robustness and amplitude fidelity remains a core bottleneck in long-horizon forecasting. While instance normalization strips time-varying mean and variance shifts to stabilize attention weights, it simultaneously erases physical scale cues required to predict extreme load peaks. Conversely, retaining raw unnormalized inputs exposes self-attention layers to severe covariate shift, causing validation error to diverge over extended horizons. Resolving this tension requires a mechanism that disentangles intrinsic temporal dynamics from transient scale drift without discarding magnitude information.

paragraphs.paragraph_intent_zh: 我这一段想在指出前人痛点后，正式亮出我们的方法（To address this dilemma, we propose...），并用最通俗清晰的直觉告诉审稿人为什么我们的设计能破局。

paragraphs.paragraph_en: To resolve this dilemma, we propose DyTS-Net, a dual-stream forecasting architecture that decouples stationary structural modeling from dynamic scale trajectory estimation. Our key insight is that while high-frequency phase relationships benefit from normalized shift-invariant attention, macro-scale amplitude evolution follows a low-dimensional continuous dynamical system. Specifically, DyTS-Net first extracts scale-invariant temporal tokens via spectral patch attention, and concurrently models non-stationary mean-variance evolution through a lightweight neural ODE branch. Recombining both streams at the decoding stage preserves sharp peak magnitudes without sacrificing training stability.

paragraphs.paragraph_intent_zh: 我这一段想说明：把我们的核心思想落地时遇到了两个具体工程/数学难点，我们分别设计了什么精巧机制去攻克它们。

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Instantiating closed-loop visuomotor diffusion on physical robots entails two technical challenges. First, because raw depth camera streams contain occlusion artifacts around reflective object edges, we introduce a tactile-guided cross-attention gate that reweights visual tokens upon contact onset. Second, to eliminate the 200 ms sampling bottleneck of iterative denoising, we formulate a trajectory consistency distillation objective that maps Gaussian noise directly to collision-free action chunks in two forward steps. Together, these designs sustain 50 Hz reactive control under partial visual occlusion.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: We evaluate DyTS-Net across eight long-horizon forecasting benchmarks and a real-world wind-turbine telemetry system spanning 1,400 sensors. Across all prediction horizons up to 720 steps, DyTS-Net reduces MSE by 12.8% over PatchTST and 17.4% over iTransformer, with the largest gains emerging during sudden weather-front transitions. Furthermore, our architecture requires 45% fewer FLOPs than full channel-mixing Transformers and transfers zero-shot to newly deployed turbine units without fine-tuning.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: In summary, our main contributions are threefold: (1) We formalize the amplitude-stationarity trade-off in long-horizon forecasting and prove that standard instance normalization bounds peak-load recoverability. (2) We propose DyTS-Net, a hybrid architecture that couples shift-invariant spectral attention with a continuous neural ODE scale tracker. (3) We demonstrate across eight public benchmarks and industrial wind-power telemetry that DyTS-Net lowers long-range MSE by up to 17.4% while cutting inference latency nearly in half.
